title: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven
hook: Yudhishthira reaches heaven and finds his old enemy enthroned there, and his brothers nowhere in sight

segments.voice: Yesterday, the dog at heaven's gate turned out to be Dharma, and Yudhishthira had refused to leave it. Your line was he will not give it up.

The chariot sets him down in heaven, and the first face Yudhishthira sees is Duryodhana's. The cousin behind the rigged game of dice. The man who had Draupadi dragged into the hall. The one who would not make peace. He sits in splendor, honored among the gods. Yudhishthira's brothers are nowhere. Draupadi is nowhere. Karna is nowhere. And the man who refused heaven's chariot rather than abandon a dog says, in effect, that he does not want this heaven. Take me to my brothers. Wherever they are, that's where I want to be.
screen: `DURYODHANA, ENTHRONED.` → `NO BROTHERS. NO DRAUPADI.` → `"TAKE ME TO THEM."`

segments.voice: The sage Narada tries to calm him: this is heaven, old quarrels end here, and Duryodhana died fighting as a warrior. Yudhishthira won't be calmed. So the gods send a messenger to guide him to his family. The path turns dark and smells of decay. Thorns, burning things, bodies, a river that scalds. It is a hell. Yudhishthira turns to go back, and voices call out of the dark. Stay, they beg. While you stand here, a cool breeze blows and our pain eases. Who are you? Karna, they answer. Bhima. Arjuna. Nakula. Sahadeva. Dhrishtadyumna. Draupadi. The sons of Draupadi. Everyone he loved is in torment, while the man who caused the war sits on a throne. Yudhishthira is furious, at the gods and at dharma itself. Then he chooses. He sends the messenger back without him: if his presence comforts them, he will stay in hell. That is the moment it ends. Indra and the gods appear, and the darkness lifts. It was an illusion, Indra explains; every king must glimpse hell, and Yudhishthira saw it because of his own deception in the war, about Drona's son. Dharma says his son has been tested once more and has held. Yudhishthira bathes in the heavenly Ganga, leaves his human body, and finds his brothers and Draupadi in their own true forms. The serial that began with a family quarrel ends with a man who would rather share his family's pain than enjoy a heaven without them.
screen: `NARADA: OLD QUARRELS END HERE` · `VOICES IN THE DARK: "STAY"` · `HE CHOOSES TO STAY IN HELL` · then, large: `THE ILLUSION LIFTS`

segments.voice: This is the end of a very long story, so give it a quiet minute. Bring to mind one person whose hard time you would rather share than be spared from, and stand near them in your mind, the way Yudhishthira stood in the dark. If you pray, hold them in your prayer; if not, simply keep them company.
Svarga. Heaven, the realm Yudhishthira reaches, and then chooses to leave for the hell where his family waits.
Your line: he will stay in hell. Tomorrow a new story begins, with a birth. That's the end of a very long road.

howItsDone: The Svargarohana Parva is the last book of the Mahabharata; Hindus hear its ending in recitations of the full epic, and some retellings of the epic linger on Yudhishthira's choice to stay with his family.

what a scholar hears: it was an illusion; Indra says every king must glimpse hell, and Yudhishthira's came from his deception about Drona's son.

chat.says: Why would Yudhishthira choose hell when he was already in heaven?
options: His family was there, and his staying eased their pain, so he stayed.
He thought hell was the real heaven, and the gods were testing his sight.
He was angry at Indra and wanted to refuse anything the gods gave him.
chat.meaning: The voices said his presence eased their pain. He chose to stay with them, and then the illusion lifted.

Duryodhana.meaning: the Kaurava cousin who would not make peace

Narada.meaning: a sage who appears across the epics and Puranas

Karna.meaning: the great warrior, the Pandavas' elder half-brother

Dhrishtadyumna.meaning: Draupadi's brother, a commander on the Pandava side

Ganga.meaning: the sacred river; here its heavenly stream

notes: All paraphrase of Ganguli; on-screen quotation marks mark glosses of speech, not quotations.
Confirm the list of voices in hell (Karna, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadi, and the sons of Draupadi).

Confirm Indra's explanation: that all kings must see hell, and that Yudhishthira was shown it because of his deception of Drona about Ashvatthama. The script says 'his own deception in the war, about Drona's son'.
Confirm Dharma's statement that this was a further test. Ganguli may number it as the third test; the number was left out.
Confirm the bath in the heavenly Ganga (Mandakini) and Yudhishthira's casting off his human body.
This is the last day of the 'Mahabharata as a serial' part; the closing sentence sums up the serial without claims about its length or date.
